Subject: Kickoff: MAP + requested perf slices (TTFT/throughput)

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, Acme wants a short mutual action plan so we can close procurement by end of May. Main asks from our side:

- A concise MAP with milestones for evaluation, legal/ procurement gating, and a recommended HW fleet that meets our latency SLOs.
- Concrete perf numbers for our workload: TTFT (time-to-first-token), p50/p95/p99 latency, sustained throughput (tokens/sec) and how those numbers change with concurrency.
- Clear guidance on MIG vs full-GPU, and A100 vs H100 vs L40S tradeoffs for both cost and predictable tail latency.

We can share a small representative prompt set (attached), but you should be able to run a short synthetic that matches our 1–2k token prompts. Our target: TTFT <= 120ms p50 for single-user interactive path, and p99 latency under 800ms at concurrency 8 for the 2k token scenario.

Pls propose the MAP timeline and what you'll deliver by next week. Attaching a starter doc.

Best,
Samira

Hi Samira —

Thanks — this is clear and aligned. Attached is a proposed MAP (ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short eval plan. Highlights:

1) MAP milestones (calendared):
   - Week 0 (Apr 19): Kickoff & dataset handoff (you did this)
   - Week 1 (Apr 20–23): Baseline perf runs (A100/H100/L40S, full GPU + 4-way MIG) using your prompt set and a matched synthetic.
   - Week 2 (Apr 26–30): Focused regressions (quantized 8-bit variants, batching & KV cache) + reliability/concurrency stress.
   - Week 3 (May 3–7): Final tuning, recommended fleet & cost model, draft contract terms for procurement.
   - Decision target: May 12 (internal approval) so procurement can finalize by EOM.

2) Deliverables:
   - perf_results_v1.csv (raw runs), a 1-page executive perf summary, HW recommendation (A/B/C options) and cost delta table.
   - A short runbook for TTFT/throughput tuning we can hand to your infra team.

3) Quick baseline expectations (from similar 2k-token workloads we run):
   - Full GPU (H100 80GB, fp16 tuned): TTFT p50 ~ 70–95ms, p99 ~ 350–650ms depending on batch. Sustained throughput (single GPU) ~ 2500–4500 tokens/sec at batch size 16.
   - A100 40GB (full): TTFT p50 ~ 110–140ms, p99 ~ 700–1,100ms for equivalent sequence length; throughput ~1800–3200 tok/s.
   - L40S (driver-optimized for inference): TTFT p50 comparable to H100 for smaller contexts but starts to lose on 2k sequences; throughput sits between A100 and H100.
   - MIG (4-way on A100/H100): predictable isolation but ~20–35% lower peak throughput and slightly better tail isolation at low concurrency.

I'll run the Week 1 baseline on a matched 2k prompt set in our lab and share raw CSV + summary by Friday Apr 23 EOD. Vivek will attach the HW comparison note.

Evelyn

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP + requested perf slices (TTFT/throughput) - HW notes

Samira / team —

Sharing a concise HW note from our Week 0 analysis (attached as hw_comparison_h100_a100_l40s.pdf). Key takeaways (numbers are approximate and will be validated with the full runs):

- H100 (80GB, TF32/AMP + triton fp16 paths): best-in-class for high-throughput 2k sequences when you need consistent tail behavior. Observed p99 ~ 300–500ms at concurrency 4–8 with batch tuning. Peak token throughput per GPU (mixed) ~ 4200 tok/s.

- A100 (40GB): lower memory headroom forces smaller batch sizes for long sequences; TTFT tends to be higher because of kernel dispatch overhead on longer contexts. p99 ranged 600–1,100ms in our synthetic at concurrency 8. Peak ~ 2600 tok/s.

- L40S: optimized PCIe inference card; for ACME's use-case (interactive + longer responses) it looks attractive cost-wise. TTFT p50 ~ 80–120ms for single connections; p99 sits in 450–800ms range depending on concurrency. Throughput sits ~3k tok/s.

- MIG vs full GPU:
   * 4-way MIG on H100/A100 provides stronger isolation for noisy neighbors and is useful when you run mixed small/medium models. But for sustained peak throughput and lowest TTFT we recommend full GPU (single tenant) on H100 for critical latency paths.
   * If ACME prefers a mix: we can recommend primary H100 full-GPU pool for interactive endpoints and a MIG-backed A100 pool for batch/async jobs to reduce cost and increase utilization.

- Quantization: int8/q4_0 types can reduce memory and slightly improve throughput but may increase TTFT variance; we'll include a regression matrix in perf_results_v1.csv.

I'll attach the full PDF with charts. Planning to join the Friday call to walk through numbers.

Vivek
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

If both are OK, we'll prioritize H100 full-GPU baseline runs this week and deliver the perf_results_v1.csv by EOD Friday (Apr 23).
